  • the northwestern Indian subcontinent, especially for writing Sanskrit and Kashmiri.

questions.question: What is the aim of 'Textual Criticism'? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• The aim of textual criticism is to reconstruct the original text of a document by comparing
  • all available manuscript copies to identify and remove transcription errors and variants. This
  • scholarly practice seeks to produce a "critical edition" of the text that is as close as
  • possible to the original wording and meaning, which can then be used for other
  • literary and historical analysis.

questions.question: Write a paragraph about the importance of manuscript libraries. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Manuscript libraries serve as irreplaceable repositories of human knowledge, acting as
  • crucial links to past civilizations. They meticulously preserve a vast range of original,
  • handwritten documents—from scientific and religious texts to personal letters,
  • diaries, and historical records—offering researchers, historians, and scholars
  • authentic, primary source materials that provide unique insights into the cultures,
  • philosophies, and daily lives of past societies. Through specialized preservation and
  • conservation techniques, these libraries safeguard fragile, aged materials from
  • physical and biological deterioration, often making them available to a global
  • audience through digitization efforts. By doing so, they not only protect irreplaceable
  • artifacts from being lost forever but also ensure that this vast collective heritage
  • remains accessible for study and can inform our understanding of the present and
  • shape the future.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write an essay on the significance of Manuscriptology. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Manuscriptology is the scientific study of handwritten documents, particularly those with
  • historical, cultural, or artistic value. This field examines the original artifacts of
  • knowledge, providing an authentic and unmediated window into the past. Through a
  • systematic process of collection, conservation, cataloging, and critical analysis,
  • manuscriptology reveals historical narratives, preserves cultural heritage, and
  • informs modern research across diverse fields. In an increasingly digital world, the
  • study of these fragile, centuries-old documents is more critical than ever, as they
  • contain irreplaceable information that risks being lost forever.
